title: Cotelligent POSH Policy — Prevention of Sexual Harassment

sections.title: Objective and Scope
paragraphs: This policy is established in compliance with the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 (POSH Act). The purpose is to provide a safe, secure, and dignified working environment free from sexual harassment for all employees, including women, men, and non-binary individuals. This policy applies to all employees, contractors, consultants, vendors, interns, and trainees of Cotelligent at all locations and while on official duty outside the office.

sections.title: Definition of Sexual Harassment
paragraphs: Sexual harassment includes any one or more of the following unwelcome acts or behaviour (whether directly or by implication): physical contact and advances, a demand or request for sexual favours, making sexually coloured remarks, showing pornography, any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of sexual nature.

The following circumstances, among other circumstances, if they occur or are present in relation to or connected with any act or behaviour of sexual harassment may amount to sexual harassment: implied or explicit promise of preferential treatment in employment, implied or explicit threat of detrimental treatment in employment, implied or explicit threat about present or future employment status, interference with work or creating an intimidating or offensive or hostile work environment, humiliating treatment likely to affect health or safety.

sections.title: Internal Complaints Committee (ICC)
paragraphs: Cotelligent has constituted an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) at each office location as required under the POSH Act. The ICC comprises: a Presiding Officer who is a senior woman employee, at least two members from amongst employees committed to the cause of women or having legal knowledge or experience in social work, and one external member from a non-governmental organization or association committed to the cause of women.

The ICC shall maintain confidentiality of all proceedings. Contact details of ICC members are shared during onboarding and displayed at the workplace. Employees can contact any ICC member to file a complaint.

sections.title: Complaint and Redressal Process
paragraphs: Any aggrieved employee who wishes to make a complaint of sexual harassment at the workplace can submit a written complaint to any member of the ICC within 3 months of the incident. The ICC may extend this period by another 3 months if satisfied that the delay was due to sufficient cause.

Upon receipt of a complaint, the ICC shall: send a copy of the complaint to the respondent within 7 working days, complete the inquiry within 90 days, submit a report of its findings to the employer within 10 days of completing the inquiry, and recommend appropriate action.

The aggrieved employee may also request conciliation before initiating an inquiry. No monetary settlement shall be made as a basis of conciliation. If a settlement is arrived at, the ICC shall record it and the inquiry shall not proceed further.

sections.title: Confidentiality
paragraphs: All proceedings of the ICC shall be kept strictly confidential. Contents of the complaint, identity of the complainant, respondent and witnesses, inquiry proceedings, recommendations of the ICC, and action taken by the employer shall not be disclosed to any third party.
Any person who contravenes confidentiality provisions shall be liable for disciplinary action as prescribed under the service rules of the organization.

sections.title: Protection against Retaliation
paragraphs: Cotelligent strictly prohibits retaliation against any employee who files a complaint, serves as a witness, or participates in an inquiry under this policy. Any act of retaliation shall be treated as a separate act of misconduct and shall be subject to disciplinary action.
Employees are encouraged to come forward and report incidents without fear of victimization.

sections.title: Consequences of Sexual Harassment
paragraphs: If the ICC concludes that the allegation of sexual harassment is proved, it may recommend: written apology, warning, reprimand or censure, withholding of promotion, withholding of pay rise or increments, terminating the respondent from service, undergoing counselling sessions, or carrying out community service.
If the allegation is malicious or false, the ICC may recommend action against the complainant as well, but this shall not deter genuine complaints.

sections.title: Awareness and Training
paragraphs: Cotelligent shall conduct awareness programs and sensitization workshops for all employees on a regular basis. All new employees shall be made aware of this policy during the induction process. The policy shall be prominently displayed at the workplace and on the company intranet.
